english_snapshot: from Gad[a], Eliasaph son of Deuel;

signals.text: Some manuscripts and parallel passages give the name as Reuel (compare Numbers 2:14).

source_text: וְ/מַטֵּ֖ה גָּ֑ד וְ/נָשִׂיא֙ לִ/בְנֵ֣י גָ֔ד אֶלְיָסָ֖ף בֶּן רְעוּאֵֽל־׃
english_snapshot: And the tribe of Gad[a], and the leader of the sons of Gad: Eliasaph son of Reuel.

signals.text: Some manuscripts or parallel passages give the father's name as Deuel (see Num 1:14).

source_text: וַ/נִּירָ֛/ם אָבַ֥ד חֶשְׁבּ֖וֹן עַד דִּיב֑וֹן וַ/נַּשִּׁ֣ים עַד נֹ֔פַח אֲשֶׁ֖רׄ עַד מֵֽידְבָֽא־־־׃
english_snapshot: And we shot at them[a]; Heshbon has perished as far as Dibon, and we laid waste as far as Nophah[b], which reaches to Medeba.

signals.text: The Hebrew of the opening clause is difficult and has been understood in several ways, including 'we overthrew them' or 'their dominion perished.'
The clause rendered 'we laid waste' is also uncertain; some take the form differently, but the context favors a verb of devastation in this victory song.

source_text: בְּנֵ֣י גָד֮ לְ/מִשְׁפְּחֹתָ/ם֒ לִ/צְפ֗וֹן מִשְׁפַּ֨חַת֙ הַ/צְּפוֹנִ֔י לְ/חַגִּ֕י מִשְׁפַּ֖חַת הַֽ/חַגִּ֑י לְ/שׁוּנִ֕י מִשְׁפַּ֖חַת הַ/שּׁוּנִֽי׃
english_snapshot: The sons of Gad by their clans: of Zephon[a], the clan of the Zephonites; of Haggi, the clan of the Haggites; of Shuni, the clan of the Shunites.

signals.text: Some English traditions read 'Ziphon' / 'Ziphionites' here (compare Genesis 46:16), but the Masoretic Text in this verse reads 'Zephon' (צפון), so 'Zephon' is retained in the main text.

source_text: בְּנֵ֣י בִנְיָמִן֮ לְ/מִשְׁפְּחֹתָ/ם֒ לְ/בֶ֗לַע מִשְׁפַּ֨חַת֙ הַ/בַּלְעִ֔י לְ/אַשְׁבֵּ֕ל מִשְׁפַּ֖חַת הָֽ/אַשְׁבֵּלִ֑י לַ/אֲחִירָ֕ם מִשְׁפַּ֖חַת הָ/אֲחִירָמִֽי׃
english_snapshot: The sons of Benjamin by their clans: of Bela[a], the clan of the Belaites; of Ashbel, the clan of the Ashbelites; of Ahiram, the clan of the Ahiramites.

signals.text: Ahiram in the Masoretic Text corresponds to 'Ahiam' in some textual traditions and English versions; the main text follows the Hebrew reading here.

source_text: כֵּ֗ן בְּנ֣וֹת צְלָפְחָד֮ דֹּבְרֹת֒ נָתֹ֨ן תִּתֵּ֤ן לָ/הֶם֙ אֲחֻזַּ֣ת נַחֲלָ֔ה בְּ/ת֖וֹךְ אֲחֵ֣י אֲבִי/הֶ֑ם וְ/הַֽעֲבַרְתָּ֛ אֶת נַחֲלַ֥ת אֲבִי/הֶ֖ן לָ/הֶֽן־׃
english_snapshot: The daughters of Zelophehad are right[a]. You must surely give them a hereditary possession among their father's brothers[b], and you shall transfer their father's inheritance to them.

signals.text: The Hebrew text has a masculine plural suffix in 'to them' at one point, but the referent in context is Zelophehad's daughters; the sense is therefore rendered with feminine referent in English.

source_text: וַ/יֵּ֨לְכ֜וּ בְּנֵ֨י מָכִ֧יר בֶּן מְנַשֶּׁ֛ה גִּלְעָ֖דָ/ה וַֽ/יִּלְכְּדֻ֑/הָ וַ/יּ֖וֹרֶשׁ אֶת הָ/אֱמֹרִ֥י אֲשֶׁר בָּֽ/הּ־־־׃
english_snapshot: The sons of Machir son of Manasseh went to Gilead and captured it[b][a], and dispossessed the Amorites who were in it.

signals.text: Hebrew has a singular verb, 'and he dispossessed,' after the preceding plural verbs. This may treat Machir's line as a collective singular, or it may reflect a textual or stylistic shift. Some translations smooth it to 'they dispossessed.'

source_text: וְ/הָיָ֨ה לָ/כֶ֧ם פְּאַת נֶ֛גֶב מִ/מִּדְבַּר צִ֖ן עַל יְדֵ֣י אֱד֑וֹם וְ/הָיָ֤ה לָ/כֶם֙ גְּב֣וּל נֶ֔גֶב מִ/קְצֵ֥ה יָם הַ/מֶּ֖לַח קֵֽדְמָ/ה־־־־׃
english_snapshot: Your southern side shall be from the wilderness of Zin along the side of Edom[b][a], and your southern border shall be from the end of the Salt Sea eastward.

signals.text: Traditionally 'the Dead Sea'; Hebrew 'the Salt Sea.'

source_text: וְ/יָרַ֤ד הַ/גְּבוּל֙ הַ/יַּרְדֵּ֔נָ/ה וְ/הָי֥וּ תוֹצְאֹתָ֖י/ו יָ֣ם הַ/מֶּ֑לַח זֹאת֩ תִּהְיֶ֨ה לָ/כֶ֥ם הָ/אָ֛רֶץ לִ/גְבֻלֹתֶ֖י/הָ סָבִֽיב׃
english_snapshot: Then the border shall go down to the Jordan[a], and its end shall be at the Salt Sea[b]. This shall be your land according to its borders all around.

signals.text: Hebrew 'the Salt Sea'; that is, the body of water commonly called the Dead Sea.
